title: Loads and the Gilbert Cell
intro: Resistors take a lot of area and give a gain that is hard to set. In integrated circuits transistors replace them.

items: Diode-connected loads: Av = -gm1/gm3 = -sqrt(mu_n*(W/L)1 / (mu_p*(W/L)3)) for PMOS diode loads (the mobilities cancel if the loads are NMOS). Small and linear, with excellent stability of gain over process.
Current-source loads: Av = -gm1 * (ro1 || ro3). Large gain but the output common-mode level is undefined without feedback (see common-mode feedback in op amps).
Active (mirror) loads: a current mirror as the load gives a single-ended output with the full differential gain, described on the Active Current Mirrors page.

blocks.text: Put two cross-coupled differential pairs on top of a third pair: the bottom pair, driven by one input, supplies the tail currents of the upper pairs, which are driven by the second input. The output current is proportional to the product of the two differential inputs. This 'four-quadrant multiplier' is used as a mixer in radio receivers and as a variable-gain amplifier.

blocks.title: Diode-connected load gain
blocks.text: A pair has (W/L)1 = 40 and diode-connected PMOS loads with (W/L)3 = 10 at equal current. mu_n is 3 times mu_p. Find the gain.
